sentences.zh: 比如，我最初用 Visual Basic 6 编写它，但每次点击按钮都要绘制所有那些小矩形，并且必须显示所有内容时，

sentences.en: it just crawled to a halt.
sentences.zh: 它简直慢得像爬一样。

sentences.en: But Flash, you can just basically like redraw everything and it's silky smooth.
sentences.zh: 但 Flash 可以让你基本上重绘一切，而且非常流畅。

sentences.en: Like, it doesn't matter how much stuff I put on screen.
sentences.zh: 无论我在屏幕上放多少东西都没关系。

sentences.en: Anyway, so I put ActionScript 3.0 at like my expert languages at one point.
sentences.zh: 总之，我一度把 ActionScript 3.0 列为我的专家级语言。

sentences.en: But anyways, yeah.
sentences.zh: 不过，好吧。

sentences.en: Yeah, so did you have anything to do with Flash?
sentences.zh: 那么，你和 Flash 有什么关系吗？

sentences.en: Did you have any involvement with Flash?
sentences.zh: 你参与过 Flash 的工作吗？

sentences.en: Flash, very little.
sentences.zh: Flash，参与很少。

sentences.en: So Flash came in when we acquired Macromedia.
sentences.zh: Flash 是我们在收购 Macromedia 时获得的。

sentences.en: So it was initially a Macromedia product and it came in through an acquisition.
sentences.zh: 所以它最初是 Macromedia 的产品，是通过收购进来的。

sentences.en: And when I came back to Adobe from Google, our CTO was big on Flash and decided that we were going to write all of the mobile products in Flash.
sentences.zh: 当我从谷歌回到 Adobe 时，我们的首席技术官非常推崇 Flash，并决定我们要用 Flash 编写所有的移动产品。

sentences.en: And we had just started this project called Adobe Revel, which was a consumer version of Lightroom and eventually kind of morphed into Lightroom Mobile.
sentences.zh: 我们当时刚启动了一个名为 Adobe Revel 的项目，它是 Lightroom 的消费者版本，最终演变成了 Lightroom Mobile。

sentences.en: So we had a plan because Revel was going to be a tablet-based product.
sentences.zh: 我们有一个计划，因为 Revel 本来打算做成一款基于平板电脑的产品。

sentences.en: So it was going to be centered around the tablet.
sentences.zh: 所以它将以平板电脑为中心。

sentences.en: And the idea was to then feed into Lightroom on desktop.
sentences.zh: 我们的想法是将其接入桌面版的 Lightroom。

sentences.en: And then Adobe had a product called Photoshop Express, which is still there in the App Store, but has very little to do with actual Photoshop.
sentences.zh: 当时 Adobe 还有一个名为 Photoshop Express 的产品，现在 App Store 里还有，但它与真正的 Photoshop 几乎没什么关系。

sentences.en: And so our thinking was to repurpose Photoshop Express since it had kind of the camera tech and stuff.
sentences.zh: 所以我们的想法是重新利用 Photoshop Express，因为它拥有相机技术之类的东西。

sentences.en: And to tailor that as the way to feed the ecosystem and get pictures into this consumer product standpoint or consumer product line.
sentences.zh: 并将其定制为接入生态系统并将图片导入这个消费级产品线的方式。

sentences.en: And so we had just started working with a team that was doing Express to morph it into what we needed.
sentences.zh: 我们刚开始与负责 Express 的团队合作，将其改造成我们需要的东西。

sentences.en: And when this mandate came down, we decided to sacrifice Express to get rewritten into Flash.
sentences.zh: 当这个指令下达时，我们决定牺牲 Express，将其重写为 Flash。

sentences.en: And so that eventually got done, and then it was like a two-year effort, and then it was scrapped.
sentences.zh: 最终完成了，那是一项为期两年的工作，然后就被废弃了。

sentences.en: What was it written in originally?
sentences.zh: 它最初是用什么编写的？

sentences.en: It was written largely in C++, so with a bit of objective C++ at the front-end side.
sentences.zh: 它主要用 C++ 编写，前端部分带有一点 Objective C++。

sentences.en: That would be a pretty big performance hit to rewriting nothing from C++ to Flash.
sentences.zh: 从 C++ 重写到 Flash，性能损失应该会非常大。

sentences.en: Yeah, but our CTO thought that that was the way of the future and that hardware would get faster, faster than it would matter.
sentences.zh: 是的，但我们的首席技术官认为那是未来之路，硬件的发展速度会快到让这些性能问题变得无关紧要。

sentences.en: And it was not the case.
sentences.zh: 但事实并非如此。

sentences.en: So Express got rewritten into Flash, and it never shipped because it took them two years to get to feature parity
sentences.zh: 所以 Express 被重写成了 Flash，但它从未发布，因为他们花了两年时间才达到两年前的功能水平，

sentences.en: to what they had two years ago, and it just was all around a worse experience.
sentences.zh: 而且整体体验更差了。

sentences.en: So that got scrapped, so we were very thankful that we didn't take Revel down that path.
sentences.zh: 所以它被废弃了，我们非常庆幸没有让 Revel 走那条路。

sentences.en: So, you know, I had some tentative involvement with Flash during those times.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，在那段时间里，我对 Flash 有过一些初步的接触。

sentences.en: And then about the time Flash was almost canceled, or about to be canceled, right?
sentences.zh: 然后大约在 Flash 快要被取消，或者即将被取消的时候，对吧？

sentences.en: For people who don't know, the reason why Flash was canceled was it just had an unbelievable stream of security issues.
sentences.zh: 对于不知道的人，Flash 被取消的原因是它有一连串令人难以置信的安全问题。

sentences.en: It was written as an old Netscape browser plug-in, and so it plugged into your browser, and that was a C API.
sentences.zh: 它是作为旧的 Netscape 浏览器插件编写的，所以它插入到你的浏览器中，那是一个 C API。

sentences.en: And so it was running outside of the sandbox, and one of the big reasons why people liked Flash is because it could give your website access to your operating system
sentences.zh: 它在沙盒之外运行，人们喜欢 Flash 的一大原因是因为它可以让你的网站访问你的操作系统

sentences.en: and your operating system capabilities.
sentences.zh: 以及你的操作系统功能。

sentences.en: The problem with that is it gave websites access to your operating system and your operating system capabilities.
sentences.zh: 问题在于，它让网站能够访问你的操作系统和操作系统功能。

sentences.en: So it became a big security problem, and there was a stream of exploits against it, and they got patched and patched and patched,
sentences.zh: 所以它成了一个巨大的安全问题，针对它的漏洞利用层出不穷，补丁打了一个又一个，

sentences.en: and that kind of sucked in so many resources it was decided that it was untenable to maintain it.
sentences.zh: 这消耗了太多的资源，以至于人们认为维护它已不可行。

sentences.en: There were a couple efforts to sandbox it or to rewrite it at the time it would have been into ASM.js and Pinnacle, which were precursors to WASM.
sentences.zh: 当时有几次尝试将其沙盒化或重写为 ASM.js 和 Pinnacle，它们是 WASM 的前身。

sentences.en: Both of those rewrites were internal, but we couldn't see a way to roll them out because being sandboxed, they cut the capabilities off from the desktop.
sentences.zh: 这两次重写都是内部进行的，但我们看不到推广它们的方法，因为一旦进入沙盒，它们就切断了与桌面的连接能力。

sentences.en: And so even though you would be able to run some sites in them, the main business that we had for Flash was not around games,
sentences.zh: 所以即使你能在其中运行一些网站，我们 Flash 的主要业务也不是围绕游戏，

sentences.en: which is how most people know Flash content, but it was around a corporate business where corporations developed their in-house applications to be written that way,
sentences.zh: 也就是大多数人所知的 Flash 内容，而是围绕企业业务，企业开发内部应用程序时会采用这种方式编写，

sentences.en: and all of those required access to the operating system.
sentences.zh: 而所有这些都需要访问操作系统。

sentences.en: And there wasn't a way to provide that without opening up a bunch of security holes.
sentences.zh: 如果不打开一大堆安全漏洞，就无法提供这种访问权限。

sentences.en: So it got killed.
sentences.zh: 所以它被砍掉了。

sentences.en: This was right at the time when the first software technology lab was in the process of being nuked.
sentences.zh: 这正好是在第一个软件技术实验室即将被裁撤的时候。

sentences.en: And there was a point there briefly where the team got redistributed, and I ended up reporting into the Flash organization, but now it was the Flash authoring tool,
sentences.zh: 当时团队被重新分配，我最终向 Flash 部门汇报，但那时已经是 Flash 创作工具了，

sentences.en: which was in the middle of a big rewrite on top of HTML5.
sentences.zh: 它正处于基于 HTML5 的大规模重写过程中。

sentences.en: And so I got assigned to that team.
sentences.zh: 所以我被分配到了那个团队。

sentences.en: What's the name of that tool?
sentences.zh: 那个工具叫什么名字？

sentences.en: Is it a product these days?
sentences.zh: 现在还有这个产品吗？

sentences.en: I think it still is.
sentences.zh: 我想应该还有。

sentences.en: I don't even know what the name of it is now.
sentences.zh: 我现在甚至不知道它叫什么名字。

sentences.en: For a while, it was just called Flash, which was very confusing because...
sentences.zh: 有一段时间，它就叫 Flash，这非常令人困惑，因为……

sentences.en: I can't imagine why.
sentences.zh: 我无法想象为什么。

sentences.en: I can't imagine why.
sentences.zh: 我无法想象为什么。

sentences.en: Yeah, yeah, yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊，是啊，是啊。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So I got assigned to that team for a little while.
sentences.zh: 所以我被分配到那个团队待了一段时间。

sentences.en: I spent less than a month consulting with them, and this was when we were trying to figure out what was going to happen with a software technology lab.
sentences.zh: 我为他们做了不到一个月的咨询，当时我们正试图弄清楚软件技术实验室会发生什么。

sentences.en: And then I had a sabbatical, and so the day before my sabbatical, I got called into a meeting
sentences.zh: 然后我休了假，就在我休假的前一天，我被叫去开会，

sentences.en: and they said, well, we wanted to have this straightened out before you left on sabbatical.
sentences.zh: 他们说，我们想在你休假前把这件事理清楚。

sentences.en: And the decision is, is we're distributing the entire team all over the company.
sentences.zh: 决定是，我们要把整个团队分流到公司各处。

sentences.en: And that's the way it's my girlfriend.
sentences.zh: 我女朋友也是这样。

sentences.en: It keeps every time before vacation, her boss, like the day before vacation, boss schedules a meeting.
sentences.zh: 每次休假前，她老板都会在休假前一天安排会议。

sentences.en: And then it's always some bad news.
sentences.zh: 然后总是些坏消息。

sentences.en: And then it's just like it ruins the whole thing.
sentences.zh: 这简直毁了整个假期。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So my sabbatical was spent looking for another job.
sentences.zh: 所以我休假期间都在找工作。

sentences.en: And so I came back and resigned.
sentences.zh: 回来后我就辞职了。

sentences.en: Was that when you went to Google?
sentences.zh: 那是你去谷歌的时候吗？

sentences.en: That was when I went to Google, yeah.
sentences.zh: 那是去谷歌的时候，没错。

sentences.en: Have we talked about Sean's time ago?
sentences.zh: 我们聊过 Sean 的那段时光吗？

sentences.en: We have, yeah.
sentences.zh: 聊过，是的。

sentences.en: That's the famous Rotate store.
sentences.zh: 那是著名的 Rotate 商店。

sentences.en: Oh, that is.
sentences.zh: 哦，没错。

sentences.en: Yeah, that's where Rotate is.
sentences.zh: 是的，Rotate 就在那里。

sentences.en: So that's the little involvement I had with Flash.
sentences.zh: 这就是我与 Flash 的一点点交集。

sentences.en: I got what I wanted out of that.
sentences.zh: 我从中得到了我想要的。

sentences.en: My thinking is like, you know, makes the Flash renaming to Flash for a different product makes Microsoft Teams new teams not seem so bad because they prefixed at least a new.
sentences.zh: 我的想法是，你知道，将 Flash 重命名为另一个产品的 Flash，让微软 Teams 的新 Teams 看起来没那么糟糕，因为他们至少加了“新”这个前缀。

sentences.en: Look, we work at NVIDIA.
sentences.zh: 听着，我们在 NVIDIA 工作。

sentences.en: I don't think we can give anybody shit about product naming because ours is pretty bad.
sentences.zh: 我觉得我们没资格吐槽别人的产品命名，因为我们自己的也很烂。

sentences.en: Tesla.
sentences.zh: Tesla。

sentences.en: We named Tesla firSt.
sentences.zh: 我们先命名了 Tesla。

sentences.en: And then, you know.
sentences.zh: 然后，你知道的。

sentences.en: Tesla at NVIDIA is the name of a business unit, a product, a microarchitecture, and like a particular GPU skew.
sentences.zh: NVIDIA 的 Tesla 是一个业务部门、一个产品、一个微架构，以及某种特定的 GPU 型号的名称。

sentences.en: Well, in my ivory tower that I do my research in, I wasn't aware of all that.
sentences.zh: 好吧，在我做研究的象牙塔里，我并不知道这一切。

sentences.en: It's actually my business unit.
sentences.zh: 那实际上是我的业务部门。

sentences.en: It was called the Tesla business unit.
sentences.zh: 它被称为 Tesla 业务部门。

sentences.en: That's what the HPC business unit was called back in the day.
sentences.zh: 那是当年高性能计算业务部门的名称。

sentences.en: Tesla was the name of the first NVIDIA, like, real compute architecture back in the day.
sentences.zh: Tesla 是 NVIDIA 当年第一个真正的计算架构的名称。

sentences.en: Well, we've got halfway through the episode and we've still got 25 minutes until Sean needs to go to his next meeting.
sentences.zh: 好吧，我们已经聊了一半了，距离 Sean 去开下一个会还有 25 分钟。

sentences.en: So maybe in the last 25 minutes, we might get to a couple more topics.
sentences.zh: 所以也许在最后 25 分钟里，我们还能再聊几个话题。

sentences.en: You can give us, we are T minus 25 minutes from Sean's next meeting, but T minus one hour and 55 minutes from the New York C++ meetup being held at the other Adobe office,
sentences.zh: 你可以告诉我们，距离 Sean 的下一个会议还有 25 分钟，但距离在另一个 Adobe 办公室举行的纽约 C++ 聚会还有 1 小时 55 分钟，

sentences.en: which we already have badges to.
sentences.zh: 我们已经有那里的入场证了。

sentences.en: Because we went there a little earlier, as you heard.
sentences.zh: 因为正如你所听到的，我们早些时候去过那里。

sentences.en: You're going to be speaking.
sentences.zh: 你要去演讲。

sentences.en: Do you want to tell us about your talk and, yeah, what you're going to be talking about?
sentences.zh: 你想跟我们说说你的演讲，还有，你要讲些什么吗？

sentences.en: Sure.
sentences.zh: 当然。

sentences.en: I'm going to be talking about, well, this is kind of a draft of a talk about a draft of a library, about half an idea.
sentences.zh: 我要讲的是，嗯，这算是一个关于某个库草案的演讲草稿，大概只有一半的想法。

sentences.en: So we'll see how this goes.
sentences.zh: 所以我们看看效果如何。

sentences.en: So I've been talking with, mostly with Eric Niebler, about senders and receivers.
sentences.zh: 我一直在和 Eric Niebler 讨论发送者和接收者（senders and receivers）。

sentences.en: I looked it up.
sentences.zh: 我查了一下。

sentences.en: It's more than eight years we've been having conversations around this.
sentences.zh: 我们围绕这个话题的讨论已经超过八年了。

sentences.en: And I built the STLAB concurrency library, which is mentioned in the sender-receiver proposal as prior work and some inspiration there.
sentences.zh: 我构建了 STLAB 并发库，它在发送者-接收者提案中被提及为先前的工作和灵感来源。

sentences.en: And I've had some issues with sender-receivers.
sentences.zh: 我对发送者-接收者有一些看法。

sentences.en: And one conversation that I've had with Eric repeatedly is at the end of the day, I think senders and receivers are just a way of doing function composition.
sentences.zh: 我和 Eric 反复讨论过的一个观点是，归根结底，我认为发送者和接收者只是一种函数组合的方式。

sentences.en: So basically all that they are, or you're doing, you're composing a bunch of functions, which then you're going to execute.
sentences.zh: 所以基本上它们所做的，或者你所做的，就是组合一堆函数，然后去执行它们。

sentences.en: And those functions describe asynchronous or concurrent operations.
sentences.zh: 这些函数描述了异步或并发操作。

sentences.en: And you're effectively building a program and then running the program.
sentences.zh: 你实际上是在构建一个程序，然后运行这个程序。

sentences.en: And it's a somewhat functional language that you're building them in.
sentences.zh: 你构建它们所用的语言是一种函数式语言。

sentences.en: But the sender-receiver interface doesn't readily expose that.
sentences.zh: 但发送者-接收者接口并没有直接体现这一点。

sentences.en: You've got, you know, some complicated concepts that have multiple interface calls on them for setting values and setting exceptions and setting stopped and getting stopped tokens.
sentences.zh: 你有，你知道的，一些复杂的概念，它们有多个接口调用，用于设置值、设置异常、设置停止以及获取停止令牌。

sentences.en: And it's this very broad interface that doesn't look like, under the hood, like just function composition.
sentences.zh: 这是一个非常广泛的接口，底层看起来并不像简单的函数组合。

sentences.en: And so a couple weeks ago, a day less than two weeks ago, I had this thought about, well, if you just took a sequence of functions and stuck them in a tuple,
sentences.zh: 所以几周前，不到两周前，我有了这个想法，如果你只取一系列函数并将它们放入元组中，

sentences.en: that you could use a fold expression to execute them flat in sequence where the result of one feeds to the argument of the next and could make that work.
sentences.zh: 你可以使用折叠表达式按顺序平铺执行它们，其中一个的结果作为下一个的参数，这样是可以实现的。

sentences.en: And so I wrote a little snippet of code to do that.
sentences.zh: 所以我写了一小段代码来做这件事。

sentences.en: And then I started to think, how do you go from there to building up the rest of the capabilities that you would have in sender-receivers?
sentences.zh: 然后我开始思考，如何从那里开始构建发送者-接收者中拥有的其余功能？

sentences.en: And got pretty far and had some insights along the way.
sentences.zh: 我进展得相当顺利，并在此过程中获得了一些见解。

sentences.en: The work certainly isn't complete at this point.
sentences.zh: 目前这项工作肯定还没有完成。

sentences.en: But it's got some interesting aspects to it in that the structure of these things, I call them chains,
sentences.zh: 但它有一些有趣的方面，因为这些东西的结构，我称之为链（chains），

sentences.en: it's really just a two-dimensional tuple of tuples under the hood.
sentences.zh: 底层其实就是一个二维的元组嵌套元组。

sentences.en: And that's maintained and exposed.
sentences.zh: 这一点得到了保留和展示。

sentences.en: The structure of them is very simple, but when you want to actually do something with them,
sentences.zh: 它们的结构非常简单，但当你真正想用它们做点什么时，

sentences.en: you can wrap an algorithm around them that transforms that structure into a new structure and then executes that new structure.
sentences.zh: 你可以围绕它们封装一个算法，将该结构转换为新结构，然后执行这个新结构。

sentences.en: And what that means is, like in sender-receivers, you would say,
sentences.zh: 这意味着，就像在发送者-接收者模型中，你会说，

sentences.en: then and hand it a lambda, and what that is in sender-receivers is what is it?
sentences.zh: 然后给它一个 lambda 表达式，而在发送者-接收者模型中，那到底是什么呢？

sentences.en: It's a sender-adapter closure, right?
sentences.zh: 那是一个发送者适配器闭包，对吧？

sentences.en: So it's taking a lambda and it's capturing it in a sender and adapting it to the sender interface
sentences.zh: 所以它接收一个 lambda 表达式，将其捕获在一个发送者中，并使其适配发送者接口，

sentences.en: and giving you back a new function, in quotes, which is a sender that accepts a sender and returns a sender.
sentences.zh: 然后给你返回一个新的函数（加引号的），它是一个接收发送者并返回发送者的发送者。

sentences.en: So it's this complicated little thing.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一个复杂的小东西。

sentences.en: And in my model, then lambda expression is just take the lambda expression and append it to the end of the tuple.
sentences.zh: 在我的模型中，lambda 表达式就是获取该 lambda 表达式并将其附加到元组的末尾。

sentences.en: So that's it.
sentences.zh: 就是这样。

sentences.en: And then all the magic happens when you go to execute this, all the transformation to execute it.
sentences.zh: 然后，当你去执行它时，所有的魔法都会发生，即执行它所需的所有转换。

sentences.en: And I think there's some significant power in there.
sentences.zh: 我认为这其中蕴含着巨大的潜力。

sentences.en: So I've shown that I can do the, you know, transfer the execution onto other threads or other execution contexts,
sentences.zh: 我已经展示了可以做到，你知道，将执行转移到其他线程或其他执行上下文中，

sentences.en: and I can inject in the transformation cancellation tokens and error handling.
sentences.zh: 并且我可以注入转换取消令牌和错误处理。

sentences.en: You know, these functions are free to throw exceptions if they want to throw exceptions.

sentences.en: It's interesting because one thing that I and to some degree Connor have been working on recently has been looking at how do we paralyze range pipelines?
sentences.zh: 这很有趣，因为我和 Connor 最近在某种程度上一直在研究如何并行化范围管道。

sentences.en: And one of the challenges with that is that if we have like a range pipeline that has a filter somewhere inside of there,
sentences.zh: 其中一个挑战是，如果我们有一个在某个地方带有过滤器的范围管道，

sentences.en: we got to go find that filter and we got to replace it with some other operation that introduces some tombstone values.
sentences.zh: 我们必须找到那个过滤器，并用一些引入墓碑值的其他操作替换它。

sentences.en: And then later we remove them.
sentences.zh: 然后稍后再删除它们。

sentences.en: And there's all sorts of other optimizations that we got to do where we have to be able to inspect the whole pipeline.
sentences.zh: 还有各种各样的其他优化，我们必须能够检查整个管道。

sentences.en: And because of the way that range pipelines are built today, which is where they're recursively, they're nested, it's a little bit harder to do this decomposition and optimization.
sentences.zh: 由于目前构建范围管道的方式是递归嵌套的，进行这种分解和优化有点困难。

sentences.en: And, you know, if instead of being this nested structure, if they were represented as like a tuple of views or a tuple of things that were going to be applied together,
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，如果它们不是这种嵌套结构，而是表示为视图元组或将要一起应用的事物元组，

sentences.en: it would be so much easier.
sentences.zh: 那会容易得多。

sentences.en: Things to be composed instead of things already composed.
sentences.zh: 让事物被组合，而不是已经组合好的事物。

sentences.en: Exactly, exactly, exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错，没错，没错。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Yeah, because like the – I think maybe the realization that we didn't have was that like with ranges,
sentences.zh: 是的，因为——我想我们可能没有意识到的是，对于范围来说，

sentences.en: the reason that they come to you already composed is because there's – you know, that there was – in the serial world, there's really just sort of one way of composing them.
sentences.zh: 它们之所以以已经组合好的形式出现，是因为——你知道，在串行世界中，组合它们的方式确实只有一种。

sentences.en: But actually – or sort of naively, there's just one way of composing them.
sentences.zh: 但实际上——或者说天真地看，组合它们的方式只有一种。

sentences.en: But actually, you might want to do optimizations or transformations or compose them in a different way, you know, apply some different thing to them.
sentences.zh: 但实际上，你可能想要进行优化或转换，或者以不同的方式组合它们，你知道，对它们应用一些不同的东西。

sentences.en: And so representing them in the uncomposed form and that gives you a lot more flexibility.
sentences.zh: 因此，以未组合的形式表示它们会给你带来更大的灵活性。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And that's what I found is you can inject, like I said, all the structure you need.
sentences.zh: 这就是我发现的，你可以注入，就像我说的，你需要的所有结构。

sentences.en: And so instead of in the sender-receiver model where you're pulling through a message for what happens if there's an exception and messages for stops and things like that,
sentences.zh: 所以，在发送者-接收者模型中，你通过消息来拉取异常发生时的情况，以及停止消息等等，

sentences.en: that interface impacts every single level all the way through the pipeline because it all has to be composed together.
sentences.zh: 那个接口会影响整个管道的每一层，因为它们都必须组合在一起。

sentences.en: If instead you say, just give me the structure, all of that information can be injected after by just transforming that structure.
sentences.zh: 如果相反，你说，只给我结构，所有这些信息都可以在之后通过转换该结构来注入。

sentences.en: And when the structure is flat, it's pretty simple to do.
sentences.zh: 当结构是扁平的时候，这很简单。

sentences.en: And since these are all – you know, it's a tuple of tuple of functions and they can be lambdas, but you could also have a type in there, which is your filter.
sentences.zh: 而且由于这些都是——你知道，它是函数元组的元组，它们可以是 lambda，但你也可以在其中放入一个类型，也就是你的过滤器。

sentences.en: And so now you can scan through the tuple of tuple and pull out particular types.
sentences.zh: 所以现在你可以扫描元组的元组并提取特定的类型。

sentences.en: So if you have additional information you want encoded in there, you can encode it in the type system and pull that out as part of the transformation.
sentences.zh: 因此，如果你有想要编码在其中的额外信息，你可以将其编码在类型系统中，并将其作为转换的一部分提取出来。

sentences.en: I wonder too if – it depends on how it was implemented, but like if you have an ability to avoid one of the worst parts of ranges, which is the errors at compile time.
sentences.zh: 我也在想——这取决于它是如何实现的，但如果你有能力避免范围最糟糕的部分之一，即编译时的错误。

sentences.en: Because like I'm even as a ranges expert and, you know, I'm not Tristan or Eric level, but, you know, I've spent quite a bit of time playing around with ranges.
sentences.zh: 因为即使作为范围专家，你知道，我不是 Tristan 或 Eric 那种水平，但你知道，我花了不少时间玩弄范围。

sentences.en: Every once in a while I'm running into my first few errors, it's just like this wall.
sentences.zh: 偶尔我会遇到我的前几个错误，就像撞到了一堵墙。

sentences.en: And it's like it's not wrong.
sentences.zh: 而且它看起来并没有错。

sentences.en: It is technically the type and it's just this nested crazy thing.
sentences.zh: 从技术上讲，它确实是那个类型，只是一个嵌套的疯狂东西。

sentences.en: You might run into the same problem, but potentially there's an opportunity to like avoid that.
sentences.zh: 你可能会遇到同样的问题，但可能有一个机会可以避免它。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: It's potential at this point.
sentences.zh: 目前这只是个潜力。

sentences.en: The error message that I most frequently get is tuple doesn't support the call operator.
sentences.zh: 我最常得到的错误信息是元组不支持调用操作符。

sentences.en: And that really means that some piece of my tuple in my fold expression is gone and it doesn't tell me.
sentences.zh: 这实际上意味着我折叠表达式中的元组的某一部分不见了，而且它没有告诉我。

sentences.en: Since it's within the fold expression, it's like one of the 20 things you have in this pipeline is bad.
sentences.zh: 因为它在折叠表达式中，就像这个管道中的 20 个东西里有一个是坏的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And that's a pain.
sentences.zh: 那很痛苦。

sentences.en: I've got some thoughts about how to – well, there's a couple of things.
sentences.zh: 我有关于如何——嗯，有几件事。

sentences.en: Right now I'm building things where everything takes, you know, auto dot dot dot as the args and – and which means you're able to build these very generic computational patterns.
sentences.zh: 现在我正在构建的东西，一切都采用，你知道，auto 点点点作为参数，这意味着你能够构建这些非常通用的计算模式。

sentences.en: But that also means when you actually call it with – you know, invoke it with 42 and something goes wrong because there's a tight mismatch in the path that you're completely loSt.
sentences.zh: 但这同时也意味着当你真正用 42 调用它时，如果因为路径中的类型不匹配而出了问题，你就完全迷失了。

sentences.en: And so one of the things I'm playing with now is what are the tradeoffs between having the developer declare the interface for the entire construct up front so that as you append each thing,
sentences.zh: 所以我现在正在尝试的一件事是，在让开发者预先声明整个结构的接口之间有什么权衡，这样当你附加每一件事时，

sentences.en: you can say, okay, if I know what the interface is, then when I append the first thing, I can see, well, will it take those arguments?
sentences.zh: 你可以说，好吧，如果我知道接口是什么，那么当我附加第一件事时，我可以看看，嗯，它会接受这些参数吗？

sentences.en: And then what does it return?
sentences.zh: 然后它返回什么？

sentences.en: And when I append the next thing, I can say, will it take the thing that's returned from the previous thing?
sentences.zh: 当我附加下一件事时，我可以看看，它会接受前一件事返回的东西吗？

sentences.en: And so on.
sentences.zh: 以此类推。

sentences.en: So I can type check the entire path.
sentences.zh: 所以我可以对整个路径进行类型检查。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Connor, I think you make a – it's a very interesting observation there.
sentences.zh: Connor，我认为你提出了一个——这是一个非常有趣的观察。

sentences.en: And I think to do better, you have to not diagnose either when you're folding or once the thing is folded.
sentences.zh: 我认为要做得更好，你必须在折叠时或折叠完成后都不要进行诊断。

sentences.en: Because the problem is that the folding operation, you end up with this recursive structure.
sentences.zh: 因为问题在于折叠操作，你最终会得到这种递归结构。

sentences.en: And then if something bad happens down deep in the structure, then it has to roll up the stack.
sentences.zh: 然后如果结构深处发生了不好的事情，它就必须回溯堆栈。

sentences.en: And even like if you don't explicitly do that, just the way the compiler diagnostics are going to work is going to tell you, well, this failed here.
sentences.zh: 即使你不显式地这样做，编译器诊断的工作方式也会告诉你，嗯，这里失败了。

sentences.en: And then this is the failure at the source.
sentences.zh: 然后这是源头的失败。

sentences.en: And then that was in this context and this context and this context.
sentences.zh: 然后那是在这个上下文中，这个上下文中，这个上下文中。

sentences.en: And it will walk up the stack trace.
sentences.zh: 它会沿着堆栈跟踪向上走。

sentences.en: But if you've got it as this linear chain of tuples,
sentences.zh: 但如果你把它作为这种线性元组链，

sentences.en: then you maybe have some other options where you can do some checking before you do the fold where you just go through each pair and say, like,
sentences.zh: 那么你可能还有其他选择，可以在进行折叠之前进行一些检查，只需遍历每一对并说，比如，

sentences.en: do these things – does the first one connect to the second one?
sentences.zh: 这些东西——第一个连接到第二个吗？

sentences.en: Does the second one connect to the third one?
sentences.zh: 第二个连接到第三个吗？

sentences.en: And that could, I think, give you better diagnostics and give you more of the flat diagnostics that you'd get from just if you were writing, like, straight imperative code.
sentences.zh: 我认为这可以为你提供更好的诊断，并提供更多像你编写直接命令式代码时会得到的扁平诊断。

sentences.en: So, yeah, I think that that has some real potential there to give you better diagnostics.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，我认为这在提供更好的诊断方面确实有一些潜力。

sentences.en: I don't know whether it will help – the other challenge that I think a lot of people have with ranges is around compilation time, but same for senders.
sentences.zh: 我不知道它是否有帮助——我认为很多人对范围的另一个挑战是编译时间，发送者也是如此。

sentences.en: I don't know that this helps you there per se because ultimately at the end of the day, you're still doing the same composition.
sentences.zh: 我不知道这是否对你有帮助，因为归根结底，你仍然在做同样的组合。

sentences.en: But I think it may really help with the diagnostics.
sentences.zh: 但我认为它可能真的有助于诊断。

sentences.en: It's very interesting.
sentences.zh: 这非常有趣。

sentences.en: I mean, I'll link in the show notes.
sentences.zh: 我是说，我会在节目笔记中链接。

sentences.en: This has nothing to do with C++, but I saw in a talk by Jose Filim, the creator of Elixir, is they have a big pipeline.
sentences.zh: 这与 C++ 无关，但我看到 Elixir 的创建者 Jose Filim 的一次演讲中，他们有一个很大的管道。

sentences.en: It's, like, not even just a library.
sentences.zh: 它甚至不仅仅是一个库。

sentences.en: It's the way the whole language works.
sentences.zh: 这就是整门语言的运作方式。

sentences.en: And they showed this little demo in an Elixir live book, I think is what they call it.
sentences.zh: 他们在一个叫 Elixir Livebook 的东西里展示了这个小演示，我想他们是这么叫它的。

sentences.en: It's like a Jupyter notebook, but they just rebranded it.
sentences.zh: 它就像 Jupyter Notebook，只不过他们换了个名字。

sentences.en: And you build up your little pipe expressions, and then if you have a problem, they just, like, in the notebook, you can, like, toggle off each one of the pipes.
sentences.zh: 你可以构建自己的小管道表达式，如果遇到问题，在笔记本里，你可以直接切换关闭每一个管道。

sentences.en: Like, if you've got a functional map or a reduction or whatever.
sentences.zh: 比如，如果你有一个函数式映射、归约或者其他什么东西。

sentences.en: And then, like, there's a little hamburger bar, and you can slide them around and stuff.
sentences.zh: 然后，有一个小汉堡菜单栏，你可以滑动它们之类的。

sentences.en: So, I was watching this, and I was like, oh, my God.
sentences.zh: 所以我当时看着这个，心想，天哪。

sentences.en: Like, when you've got a problem in C++ with ranges, it's just like, you know, a wall of template mess.
sentences.zh: 在 C++ 中处理范围（ranges）问题时，就像面对一堵模板乱码墙一样。

sentences.en: Whereas over in this dynamically typed language, they're like, well, check out this little demo of debug.
sentences.zh: 而在这门动态类型语言里，他们却说，嘿，看看这个调试演示。

sentences.en: And, like, you could, as the final thing, you could pipe it to, like, a debug print or something.
sentences.zh: 你可以把最后一步通过管道传给调试打印之类的东西。

sentences.en: And then in the notebook, it shows you at every stage, like, what the current, you know, value.
sentences.zh: 然后在笔记本里，它会在每个阶段向你展示当前的值。

sentences.en: Anyways, it was just amazing.
sentences.zh: 总之，这太神奇了。

sentences.en: So, I'm not saying we're ever going to get to that, but there is hope out there that, you know, things can be better.
sentences.zh: 我不是说我们一定能做到那样，但至少让人看到了一线希望，事情是可以变得更好的。

sentences.en: And, you know, that's why we have you on the show, so we can give you a bunch of work, Sean.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么我们要请你上节目，这样我们就能给你派一堆活儿了，Sean。

sentences.en: Yeah, you're going to go write a C++ committee paper, of course, and give us full reference implementation.
sentences.zh: 没错，你当然得去写一份 C++ 委员会提案，还要给我们提供完整的参考实现。

sentences.en: Sure.
sentences.zh: 没问题。

sentences.en: And, you know, first, now that you've got me thinking about this idea, I'm going to go write a C++ interpreter just so we can do this.
sentences.zh: 而且，既然你让我有了这个想法，我打算去写一个 C++ 解释器，这样我们就能实现这个功能了。

sentences.en: That'll be a good weekend project, I'm sure.
sentences.zh: 我相信那会是个很棒的周末项目。

sentences.en: So, I got a great thing for us to close on.
sentences.zh: 我有个很棒的话题来结束今天的节目。

sentences.en: All right.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: We were talking about this the other day, too.
sentences.zh: 我们前几天也聊过这个。

sentences.en: It's C++ 20 concepts is too unsafe for anyone under the age of 18.
sentences.zh: C++ 20 的概念（concepts）对 18 岁以下的人来说太不安全了。

sentences.en: So, I apologize to our younger listeners out there that are paying the $20 a month.
sentences.zh: 所以我向那些每月支付 20 美元的年轻听众道歉。

sentences.en: If you're a younger listener, please hang up now.
sentences.zh: 如果你是年轻听众，请现在挂断。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: But, yeah, what do we make of this?
sentences.zh: 但是，我们该怎么看待这件事呢？

sentences.en: We talked about this last time I was on.
sentences.zh: 我上次来的时候我们就聊过这个。

sentences.en: I mean, it's no surprise that this is coming.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这并不令人意外。

sentences.en: For corporations, I think there's going to be some amount of risk management that has to go on, and Adobe's certainly in that boat.
sentences.zh: 对于企业来说，我认为必然会有一定程度的风险管理，Adobe 当然也身处其中。

sentences.en: My team's on the hook for developing the roadmap, the memory safety roadmap for Adobe, and how we approach that.
sentences.zh: 我的团队负责制定 Adobe 的路线图，即内存安全路线图，以及我们如何处理这个问题。

sentences.en: I had an absolutely terrifying meeting with our security team yesterday on this very topic.
sentences.zh: 昨天我和我们的安全团队开了一个非常可怕的会议，讨论的正是这个话题。

sentences.en: Yeah, I mean, I think the information coming out of the Department of Defense and the White House is filled with a lot of hyperbole, but at the base of it, it's not wrong.
sentences.zh: 是的，我认为来自国防部和白宫的信息充满了夸大其词，但从根本上说，它们并没有错。

sentences.en: Just, you know, in working on this chain library at one point, I accidentally wrote T instead of decay type T.
sentences.zh: 就在我研究这个链式库的时候，我曾不小心把 T 写成了 decay_t<T>。

sentences.en: And the result was I captured a reference instead of a value, even though the code looked like it was fine, the type was not.
sentences.zh: 结果就是我捕获了一个引用而不是值，尽管代码看起来没问题，但类型不对。

sentences.en: And that meant that I had a use-after return on my stack, and it cost me half a day to debug the thing.
sentences.zh: 这意味着我的栈上出现了返回后使用（use-after-return）的问题，我花了大半天时间才调试出来。

sentences.en: Hear that, folks?
sentences.zh: 听到了吗，各位？

sentences.en: The luminary.
sentences.zh: 这位大咖。

sentences.en: Sean Harris.
sentences.zh: 肖恩·哈里斯。

sentences.en: Debugging his problem for half a day.
sentences.zh: 调试他的问题花了大半天。

sentences.en: There's hope for all of us.
sentences.zh: 我们大家都有希望了。

sentences.en: Yeah, so it's too easy to make a mistake like that, and a lot of times the wrong code looks better than the right code, and that's a problem, and this was one of those cases.
sentences.zh: 是的，犯这种错误太容易了，而且很多时候错误的代码看起来比正确的代码更好，这就是问题所在，而这正是其中一个案例。

sentences.en: There are some people that are either trying to define a safe subset of C++ or tools or things to make C++ safe or who claim that C++ is safe.
sentences.zh: 有些人试图定义 C++ 的安全子集，或者开发工具来让 C++ 变得安全，又或者声称 C++ 本身就是安全的。

sentences.en: Do you buy the argument that C++ is fundamentally unsafe and that there's no hope for it?
sentences.zh: 你认同 C++ 从根本上是不安全的，而且对此毫无希望的观点吗？

sentences.en: Or do you think that people in environments that care about safety can find a way to continue using languages like C++?
sentences.zh: 还是你认为在重视安全的环境中，人们能找到继续使用像 C++ 这样的语言的方法？

sentences.en: It's just a matter of defining the rules and the guidelines to make it, to define a safe form of C++.
sentences.zh: 这只是定义规则和指南的问题，从而定义出一种安全的 C++ 形式。

sentences.en: So I think there's like Herb Sutter's C++, which he states that one of his goals is not provable safety, but my team's looked at his proposals, and we've given him some feedback.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为有 Herb Sutter 的 C++，他声称他的目标之一不是可证明的安全性，但我的团队研究了他的提案，并给他提供了一些反馈。

sentences.en: We actually think he's very close to being able to prove safety.
sentences.zh: 我们实际上认为他非常接近于能够证明安全性。

sentences.en: He wouldn't have to compromise much to be able to do that.
sentences.zh: 他不需要做出太多妥协就能做到这一点。

sentences.en: He doesn't seem interested in it at the moment, but maybe that will change with the current legislation.
sentences.zh: 他目前似乎对此不感兴趣，但也许随着当前的立法，情况会发生变化。

sentences.en: I think the work that Sean Baxter has been doing is very promising, but of course that's one guy on a non-open source project.
sentences.zh: 我认为 Sean Baxter 所做的工作非常有前景，但当然，那是一个人做的非开源项目。

sentences.en: I hope something comes out of it, if nothing more than other people steal ideas from it.
sentences.zh: 我希望它能有所成果，哪怕只是让别人从中窃取灵感也好。

sentences.en: We talk a lot about memory safety in the abstract, both without a clear definition of memory safety is and losing sight of what the goals of the memory safety are.
sentences.zh: 我们经常在抽象层面谈论内存安全，既没有明确定义什么是内存安全，也忽略了内存安全的目标是什么。

sentences.en: And safety properties in general are tools to help prove correctness of code.
sentences.zh: 安全属性通常是帮助证明代码正确性的工具。

sentences.en: And to prove partial correctness of an application, you have to demonstrate that it satisfies a set of safety properties.
sentences.zh: 要证明应用程序的部分正确性，你必须证明它满足一组安全属性。

sentences.en: And memory safety being one of those.
sentences.zh: 内存安全就是其中之一。

sentences.en: But the goal from a security standpoint is something called a non-interference property, which is both a safety and likeness property,
sentences.zh: 但从安全角度来看，目标是所谓的“非干扰属性”（non-interference property），它既是安全性属性也是活性属性，

sentences.en: and the memory safety is just in support of non-interference.
sentences.zh: 而内存安全只是为了支持非干扰。

sentences.en: And the basic idea with non-interference is that a defect in one piece of your code should not affect another piece of your code.
sentences.zh: 非干扰的基本思想是，代码中某一部分的缺陷不应影响另一部分。

sentences.en: It should limit the blast radius.
sentences.zh: 它应该限制爆炸半径。

sentences.en: So when you're really talking about non-interference properties, things like shared pointers become a problem.
sentences.zh: 所以当你真正谈论非干扰属性时，像共享指针这样的东西就成了问题。

sentences.en: Any shared mutable state becomes a problem.
sentences.zh: 任何共享的可变状态都会成为问题。

sentences.en: Sharing indices to the same array is another way to share information becomes a problem, right?
sentences.zh: 共享指向同一个数组的索引是另一种共享信息的方式，这也会成为问题，对吧？

sentences.en: So even if you're outside of the pointer space.
sentences.zh: 所以即使你不在指针空间内也是如此。

sentences.en: And C++ doesn't give you any tools to help you build code that satisfies a non-interference property.
sentences.zh: 而 C++ 没有提供任何工具来帮助你构建满足非干扰属性的代码。

sentences.en: Even if you could go through with C++ and you could say, every place where it's undefined behavior, I'm going to insert a runtime check.
sentences.zh: 即使你可以在 C++ 中遍历代码，并说：在每一个未定义行为的地方，我都要插入一个运行时检查。

sentences.en: And ta-da, C++ is completely safe.
sentences.zh: 然后，当当，C++ 就完全安全了。

sentences.en: Your program will probably never terminate because it will run so slow, but it will be very safe.
sentences.zh: 你的程序可能永远不会终止，因为它运行得太慢了，但它会非常安全。

sentences.en: So at one end, that's completely doable.
sentences.zh: 所以从一端来看，这是完全可行的。

sentences.en: And then the next end is how much performance can you get back through optimization knowing that some of these checks are unnecessary?
sentences.zh: 而另一端是，在知道其中一些检查是不必要的情况下，通过优化能找回多少性能？

sentences.en: And then how do you structure your code to guarantee that those optimizations kick in?
sentences.zh: 然后你如何构建代码以保证这些优化生效？

sentences.en: And what are the guidelines for that?
sentences.zh: 以及相应的指导原则是什么？

sentences.en: But then you're still left with a piece of code that looks like a piece of C++ code and probably needs a redesign.
sentences.zh: 但即便如此，你剩下的代码看起来仍然像是一段 C++ 代码，而且可能需要重新设计。

sentences.en: And when they're talking about memory safety, it's 70% of the exploitable CVEs, according to Microsoft and Google, that they see.
sentences.zh: 当人们谈论内存安全时，根据微软和谷歌的数据，70% 的可利用 CVE 漏洞都与此有关。

sentences.en: Well, that leaves another 30% of the problem.
sentences.zh: 好吧，那还剩下 30% 的问题。

sentences.en: So even if we fixed all the memory safety problems, we wouldn't have like super bulletproof software.
sentences.zh: 所以即使我们解决了所有的内存安全问题，我们也不会拥有那种超级防弹的软件。

sentences.en: You know, it's like your ship's going down.
sentences.zh: 你知道，就像你的船正在下沉。

sentences.en: It's got three holes in it.
sentences.zh: 上面有三个洞。

sentences.en: And you're like, well, we got a way to patch two of them.
sentences.zh: 然后你说，好吧，我们有办法补上其中两个。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Right?
sentences.zh: 对吧？

sentences.en: Well, and also if everybody's programming memory safe languages, then attackers will – it will spur innovation and new ways of attacking software.
sentences.zh: 而且，如果每个人都在用内存安全的语言编程，那么攻击者也会——这会刺激创新和攻击软件的新方法。

sentences.en: There will always be attacks.
sentences.zh: 攻击永远都会存在。

sentences.en: Yeah, there will always be attacks.
sentences.zh: 是的，攻击永远都会存在。

sentences.en: So I think eventually the changes have to be, you know, much deeper and much more radical than just shoring up C++.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为最终这些改变必须比仅仅加固 C++ 更深入、更彻底。

sentences.en: That said, Photoshop alone has 30 million lines of C++ code.
sentences.zh: 话虽如此，仅 Photoshop 就有 3000 万行 C++ 代码。

sentences.en: And it's not going away anytime soon.
sentences.zh: 而且它短期内不会消失。

sentences.en: How long did you say that flash rewrite took?
sentences.zh: 你说 Flash 重写花了多久？

sentences.en: You know, two years?
sentences.zh: 你知道，两年？

sentences.en: How many lines was that probably, you know?
sentences.zh: 那大概有多少行代码，你知道吗？

sentences.en: I don't know.
sentences.zh: 我不知道。

sentences.en: Maybe 500,000 tops.
sentences.zh: 最多 50 万行吧。

sentences.en: So that's like a factor of 30 million carried.
sentences.zh: 所以那是 3000 万行的 1/60。

sentences.en: I think it's just two.
sentences.zh: 我觉得只有 2。

sentences.en: So it's like four years is all you need.
sentences.zh: 所以你只需要四年时间。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Good math there.
sentences.zh: 数学算得真好。

sentences.en: We should probably let Sean go because he's got another meeting.
sentences.zh: 我们大概得放 Sean 走了，因为他还有个会。

sentences.en: This is true.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: We have made you late.
sentences.zh: 我们让你迟到了。

sentences.zh: 我一直听到我的手表在震动。

sentences.zh: 感谢收听。
